key_insight: Frozen visual world models for Atari Pong often fail to preserve task-critical concepts like the ball, and concept-guided spatial regularization can partially reduce these failures.
engineering_relevance: For model-based RL systems, improving the fidelity of internal world dynamics can materially affect downstream policy quality, so diagnostics beyond training return are essential.
method: Reproduced five visual world-model agents: DreamerV3, DIAMOND, TWISTER, Simulus, and STORM.
Evaluated frozen models with closed-loop rollouts using separately trained policies to expose visual and dynamical errors.
Introduced Concept-Guided Spatial Regularization (CGSReg), an auxiliary pixel reconstruction loss on segmented concept regions.
evidence_signal: Across all five models, rollouts showed failures such as ball disappearance and invalid ball-paddle interactions, and zero-shot policies trained inside frozen models underperformed the original MBRL pipelines (e.g., DreamerV3 mean return -5.5 to -20.9).
watch_item: CGSReg improves several models but not consistently across all metrics, suggesting that concept-aware reconstruction alone does not eliminate broader world-model bottlenecks.
paper_title: Concept-Guided Spatial Regularization for World Models in Atari Pong
